about.title: Monterey Park Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Monterey Park households rely on countless everyday products — kitchen appliances, tools, vehicles, children's items, and machinery used along busy corridors like Garfield Avenue and Atlantic Boulevard. When one of those products is designed poorly, manufactured incorrectly, or sold without adequate warnings, the resulting injury can be sudden and serious. California law generally allows injured residents to pursue a strict liability claim, meaning the focus is on the defect and the harm it caused rather than proving a manufacturer was careless. That distinction matters for families in Monterey Park who are already dealing with medical bills and recovery. Our team reviews what happened, helps identify who along the supply chain may share responsibility, and explains next steps in plain language, at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Monterey Park Residents Choose Us

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Under California law, you often don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — showing the product was defective and caused your injury may be enough.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which expands who we can investigate on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Our team can advise you early on how to keep the defective item intact, since it often serves as central evidence in a strict liability claim.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California generally applies strict liability to defective product claims, meaning the injured person typically needs to show the product was defective and that the defect caused their injury. We can evaluate the specifics of your situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the condition it was in when the injury occurred, including packaging, instructions, and any broken pieces. This evidence is often central to a product liability claim, so avoid repairing or discarding it before speaking with us.

items.question: Is this connected to traffic crashes reported in Monterey Park?
items.answer: Not directly — Monterey Park's crash data (like collisions along Garvey Avenue or SR-60) generally involves auto-accident claims, while product liability covers injuries from defective goods themselves, such as a malfunctioning car part or appliance. If a vehicle defect contributed to a crash, both areas of law could potentially apply, and we can help sort that out.

items.question: Is there a cost to have us review my case?
items.answer: No. We provide free case reviews, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
